deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1983 Teichmüller notes Grothendieck builds a 'Teichmüller tower'. This is a system of topological Teichmüller groupoids T^±_{g,ν}, their variants $T^±_{g,ν} (decorated or 'rigidified', the meaning of the $ sign is unclear), and groupoids T^±_top(Γ) indexed by rigid fundamental graphs Γ. The system is linked by seven 'operations': cutting and gluing along circles, forgetting or adding boundary components, and so on. These are the Lego operations later announced in the Esquisse d'un programme.

What this page says:
(1) The operations just discussed are 'relatively superficial'. The word is probably 'bordage', i.e. operations on boundary circles. They never connect T_{g,ν} to T_{g',ν'} with g' < g.
(2) To descend in genus one needs operation 5°. This acts on the boundary circles, which are 'former gluing circles'. In modern terms it is self-gluing of two boundary components, T_{g-1,ν+2} → T_{g,ν}. This is the non-genus-preserving clutching that links the genus strata of the tower, as with clutching maps of the boundary of M̄_{g,n}.
(3) He proposes a further structure to make explicit. For each object (X,[E],R) with R ≠ ∅, take the fundamental groupoid Π_1(X;R) with base points in the set R (boundary components, i.e. tangential base points). It is functorial in R. It should commute with the operations; for gluing, a van Kampen-type gluing of groupoids is needed. Coverings X' → X should also be accounted for.
(4) Together these would give a new object: a groupoid Ŝ T^±_top fibred over the Teichmüller groupoids. Its fibres would be the Π_1(X;R). Equivalently, the margin says, a functor Ŝ T^±_top → D^±_top compatible with the operations. In other words, a strictly functorial action of the whole Teichmüller tower on the fundamental groupoids of the surfaces, compatible with gluing.
(5) Already for the simplest piece, S_2 T_{0,3} (pants), the question is non-trivial. He suspects the demand is too ambitious. The next page explains why: a strict model would have to contain 'all curves'. So he retreats to models in low dimension.

Modern reading: this is the topological backbone of Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory. Mapping-class groupoids act on fundamental groupoids of surfaces with base points on boundary or at tangential points, compatibly with the modular-operad (Lego) gluing structure. The worry about a model 'containing all curves' is a strictification/coherence problem, i.e. size issues in making a pseudo-functor strict.
errors: No mathematical error; the page is programmatic. The worry that a strict model must contain 'all curves' is a set-theoretic/strictification issue. It is solvable up to equivalence by using skeletal or combinatorial models (pants decompositions, ribbon graphs), as Grothendieck himself suggests on the next page.
The status of D^±_top and the precise meaning of the prefixes $, S, Ŝ cannot be determined from this page alone.

ideas.what: Operations on the Teichmüller tower: the boundary ('bordage') operations preserve genus; one needs a self-gluing operation (5°) of boundary circles to descend in genus
ideas.modern_name: Lego/modular-operad structure of mapping class groupoids; clutching morphisms M_{g-1,n+2} → M̄_{g,n}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984); formalized by Moore–Seiberg, Bakalov–Kirillov, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps (2000), Getzler–Kapranov (modular operads, 1998)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, Lego, 'two-level' principle)

ideas.what: Fundamental groupoid Π_1(X;R) with a set R of base points on boundary circles, functorial in R and compatible with gluing (van Kampen)
ideas.modern_name: fundamental groupoid on several (tangential) base points; groupoid van Kampen theorem
ideas.usually_credited_to: R. Brown (groupoid van Kampen, 1967); Deligne (tangential base points, 1989)
ideas.where_published: SGA1 (fundamental groupoids with several base points); Esquisse mentions tangential base points

ideas.what: A fibred object Ŝ T^±_top over the Teichmüller groupoids whose fibres are the fundamental groupoids, compatible with all tower operations (i.e. a strict functorial action of the tower on Π_1 of surfaces, including coverings X' → X)
ideas.modern_name: action of the mapping-class modular operad on the fundamental-groupoid operad; universal curve π_1(M_{g,n+1}) → π_1(M_{g,n}); GT acting compatibly on both
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara, Drinfeld, Nakamura, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Hain–Matsumoto; operadic versions by Fresse, Horel, Boavida–Horel–Robertson
ideas.where_published: Esquisse discusses the tower and the Galois action but not, as far as I know, this explicit fibred 'Ŝ T' object of fundamental groupoids

ideas.what: Recognition that a strict functorial model is 'too ambitious' (it must contain all curves), with a retreat to low-dimensional models
ideas.modern_name: strictification/coherence of pseudo-functors; skeletal combinatorial models
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (Mac Lane coherence; Pursuing Stacks themes)

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates, as an explicit target, a single fibred object combining the Teichmüller groupoid tower with the fundamental groupoids Π_1(X;R) of the surfaces themselves, compatible with all gluing operations and with coverings X' → X. This is a 'total space' version of the tower. He notes it is already non-trivial for the pants case T_{0,3} and leaves it open.
missed.quote: c'est celle donnée par le groupoïde fondamental Π_1(X;R) ... pour R≠∅, points-bases dans R ... d'un nouvel objet des groupoïdes Ŝ T^±_top. Déjà dans le cas de S_2T_{0,3} la question se pose et n'est pas triviale
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Modern GT theory treats M_{g,n} tower actions and the action on π_1 of curves largely separately, or via the universal-curve fibration with tangential base points. An explicit modular-operadic object including the fibre groupoids and covering maps, with a GT-action, is close to but not identical with existing operadic work (Horel, Boavida–Horel–Robertson in genus 0). It documents that Grothendieck conceived the combined structure in 1983.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is programmatic and its themes (Lego operations, genus-changing gluing, fundamental groupoids with boundary base points) are well known from the Esquisse and later work. The explicit wish for a functorial fibred object Ŝ T including Π_1(X;R) and coverings is a mildly interesting unpublished detail, but he immediately judges it too ambitious.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'opérations de bouclage' is more likely 'opérations de bordage' (consistent with 'le bordage' on the previous page); likewise 'cercles de bouclage' is likely 'cercles de bordage'.
'opération (5°) de grumage' is uncertain; the word may be 'gommage' or similar. The parenthetical '(= ex-cercles de recollement!)' is correctly read.
'Π_1(X;R)' is written above 'groupoïde fondamental' and replaces the struck 'des'; the following text reads '(X,[E],R), pour R≠∅, points-bases dans R'.
'X'' is inserted above 'revêtement de X', i.e. 'revêtement X' de X'.
The final 'S_2T_{0,3}' appears as a script-S symbol with subscript 2 before T_{0,3}; the reading is uncertain.
The left-margin note ends with 'i.e. foncteurs ŜT^±_top → D^±_top' (or similar); the remaining marginal words are uncertain.
